preface.para: This handbook provides information required by the user units for operations, upkeep, fault diagnosing at site. It also has a special section for use as a comprehensive asset book for maintaining record of vital data for future analysis with a view to optimize the requirement of spares and for improving its performance. It is prepared as a compendium containing the required information to accept, operate and maintain the equipment. It is aimed to assist the users of the equipment in getting acquainted with, learning about and as a day to day operating log of a given set.

Though this handbook covers main aspects of the equipment to understand capabilities, limitations, and ways to operate it, is not a supplement for on-the-job training and for assessing functional serviceability of the equipment. It is recommended to have formal training and practice before the equipment is entrusted to a completely new operating crew. Systems have been described to understand the way systems function and not merely to perform drills; so that through experience gained, users can suggest improvement besides commenting on shortcomings.

The handbook incorporates individual chapters about the basic bridging system, the technical and operating data of the bridging system, the basic operating modes, details about Bridge Superstructure, Launching Mechanism, Hydraulic System, Electrical System, the operations associated with the launching, de-launching, retrieval when damaged, inspection, care and maintenance of the equipment, as well as the historical record of operations performed by the system and the modifications carried out to it.
In designing the layout of the handbook, effort has been made to simplify the textural contents for the first time reader by adopting suitable colours, fonts and formats.

clause.title: General
clause.para: Modular Bridge (MB) as shown in Figure 1 is a complex multidisciplinary mechanically launched single span mobile bridging system with maximum span of 46m. It is used to traverse a dry / wet gap in the path of the moving platoon / regiment if the need arises. It is designed to support crossing over of tracked and wheeled vehicles up to MLC-70 load class. It is used for deploying across gaps of varying lengths as required from 14 m to 46 m. It provides a safe 4 m roadway passage for traffic across gaps and trenches. The system is transported on 10x10 and 8x8 High Mobility Vehicles (HMVs). A single span bridge of 46 m is constructed in 90 minutes in day time with the help of six (6) plus one (1) crew members. The major advantage of this system is that, it is modular in design which enables the bridge to be deployed in different spans with independent of gap depth and also for high mobility transportation.

item.text: The bridge is launched in simply supported condition irrespective of wet and dry gap in min. time span of 90 minutes in day and 120 minutes in night with seven (7) crew members.
A special hydraulic circuit is designed to facilitate launching the bridge in tactical region with temperature ranging from 0 °C to 45 °C.
Bridge is capable to launch / retrieval from either banks without any additional site preparation.
The bridge is capable to deployed in 3 m upslope and 3 m downslope for movement of vehicles.
Two (2) power sources, PTO and APU are provided in the system as inbuilt redundancy power source.
The bridge is deployed from 14 m to 46 m length in the span of approx. 6.5 m.
Two (2) launching vehicles are provided for redundancy, and for small ditch two (2) bridges can be launched simultaneously.
Equipment is capable of performing under sandy / dusty / hot environment / corrosive atmosphere of seacoast.

clause.title: System Description
clause.para:
The one (1) set of MB comprises the major subsystem like launching system, nose system, bridging system and carrier vehicles. The complete launching mechanism is mounted on
HMV 10x10. Nose superstructure comprises NEM, NCM and BSB. The Bridge superstructure comprises of BEM, BCM and Ramp assembly. All the nose and bridge superstructures transported on HMV 8x8 carrier vehicles.

clause.title: Nose Superstructure
clause.para: At time of bridge launching only one bank of gap is assessable to the crew. Therefore, a light weight launching nose assembly shown in Figure 6 and Figure 7 has to be initially launched in cantilever mode to bridge the gap. The nose superstructure provides the structural framework and stability for launching the bridge modules. The counter-moment for the dead weight of the launch Nose and other launch loads has to be provided by the weight of the launcher vehicle. Once the Nose assembly has been placed across the gap, it is used for launching of the heavier bridge assembly. Four (4) no. of nose pushing pin is provided with each nose module so that the pushing bracket arrangement provided with launching platform can push the nose modules towards the far bank and pull the nose modules during retrieval.

The nose modules are provided with chequered plates for launching crew movement during launching operation. Two (2) adjacent nose modules are locked manually with locking mechanism while launching operation. For locking nose modules, arrangement of male and female jaws are provided. There are two (2) types of nose modules NCM and NEM, refer
Figure 6 and Figure 7. These modules are carried on the carrier vehicle to the site of bridge installation. The modules are assembled and launched using launcher vehicle. Lifting hook arrangement is provided to lift nose modules with the help of MHD. Refer Table 6 for subassemblies nose superstructure.

During the launching operations, initially the NEM is connected to the BSB through a connecting pin arrangement and placed on the launching Platform. Then NCM is aligned and locked with NEM on the launching platform. The both modules push forward towards the far bank. Using the nose pushing cylinder and friction lock cylinder provides necessary locks during launching. Similarly, all remaining NCM and NEM are aligned and locked.

Once the NEM reaches the far bank the complete assembly is lowered to rest on BSB at far bank. After that the NEM in the home bank is lowered and joined with home bank BSB. Hereafter the bridge modules are placed and pushed on the nose modules. The bridge modules are docked and locked together and pushed forward on the nose modules to reach the far bank. Once the bridge modules are launched the nose modules is lowered by retracting BSB cylinder, this is to ensure sufficient gap between bridge and nose modules to support in before tank passing operation.

clause.title: Nose End Module (NEM) Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 9 and Figure 7 for Nose End module (NEM). NEM construction is tapered with provision for connection of BSB and nose extension assembly at one end. Chequered plates are provided for easy crossing the gap by crew after deploying of nose modules. The flat end of NEM is provided with male and female jaws and locking mechanism. The far bank NEM is pre-assembled with the BSB to eliminate its assembly time. Nose extension assembly is attached with home bank NEM. BSB is attached with far bank NEM. During launching operation, NEM moves forward with the help of roller assembly along with pushing pin. One (1) set of MB comprises four (4) nos. of NEM however for formation of one bridge span two (2) nos. of NEM are used.
One (1) NEM comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 7.

Refer Figure 8 for jaws. NEM is provided with two (2) types of jaws male and female. For connecting the adjacent nose module in deployment, these jaws are locked with the help of locking pin. Refer Figure 9 for location of jaws.

clause.title: Locking Screw Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 10 for locking screw mechanism. Locking screw assembly is mounted on flat side of NEM, refer Figure 9 for location of locking screw. For locking / unlocking of nose modules in desired direction screw mechanism is provided. Adjacent nose modules are locked by inserting locking pin in male and female jaws, refer Figure 11. The screw assembly can be operated from both sides. When the screw is rotated, the nut of the box section moves it with the locking pin in desired direction for locking/unlocking. For operating the screw, a square slot crank lever is provided, refer Figure 24.

clause.title: Guide Beak Assembly (Male-Female)
clause.para: Refer Figure 12 for guide beak assembly. Guide beak assembly is mounted on flat side of NEM, refer Figure 9. It is used for correct locking and to avoid misalignment during docking operation with adjacent nose modules, refer Figure 11. Guide beak assembly comprises male and female guide beak.

clause.title: Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 13 for roller assembly. Four (4) nos. of roller assemblies are fitted on the nose modules so that the nose modules slide through the rails of the launching platform, with least resistance. Purpose of the rollers is to hold the nose in position and guide it during its deployment in overhang condition. Refer Figure 9 and Figure 11 for location of roller assembly. Two (2) nos. of combi bearing are fitted in each roller assembly.

clause.title: Nose Extension Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 14 for nose extension assembly. Nose extension assembly is used to connect NEM and launching system at home bank during bridge modules launching operation. This assembly acts as rigid link between NEM and launching system. This assembly provide the support to rollers in bridge modules during bridge launching operation. During bridge launching operation stability of nose system is achieved by nose extension assembly. Refer Figure 9 for location of nose extension assembly.

clause.title: Nose Centre Module (NCM) Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 15 for Nose Centre module (NCM). NCM is provided with male / female arrangement of jaws and locking mechanisms at both the ends diagonally opposite for connecting adjacent modules. Chequered plates are provided over the surface of NCM. Four (4) numbers of nose pushing pins are provided with each NCM to push / pull as per operation. NCM slide over rails of launching platform with roller assembly. Five (5) nos. of NCMs are in one set of MB. For formation of 46 m span five (5) nos. of NCM are required. Refer Figure 6 for location of NCM.
One NCM comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 8.

Refer Figure 8 for jaws. NCM is provided with two (2) types of jaws male and female on both sides of module at top and bottom. For connecting the adjacent nose modules in deployment, these jaws are locked with the help of locking pin. Refer Figure 15 for location of jaws.

clause.title: Locking Screw Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 10 for locking screw mechanism. Two (2) nos. of locking screw assembly is mounted on both side of NCM diagonally, refer Figure 15 for location of locking screw. For locking / unlocking of nose modules in desired direction screw mechanism is provided. The nose modules are locked with each other to obtain various length of launching nose assembly with the help of locking mechanism. Adjacent nose modules are locked by inserting locking pin in male and female jaws, refer Figure 11. The screw is rotated from both sides. When the screw is rotated, the nut of the box section moves it with the locking pin in desired direction for locking/unlocking. For turning the screw, a square slot handle is provided, refer Figure 24.

clause.title: Guide Beak Assembly (Male-Female)
clause.para: Refer Figure 12 for guide beak assembly. NCM comprises of two (2) sets of guide beak assembly. Guide beak is mounted on both side of NCM diagonally, to facilitate correct locking and to avoid misalignment during docking operation with adjacent nose modules. Guide beak is constructed in two (2) parts as male and female guide beak. Refer Figure 15 for location of guide beak assembly.

clause.title: Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 13 for roller assembly. Four (4) nos. of roller assemblies are fitted on the nose modules so that the nose modules slide through the rails of the launching platform, with least resistance. The main purpose of the rollers is to hold the nose in position and guide it during its deployment in overhang condition. Refer Figure 11 Figure 15 for location of roller assembly. There are two (2) nos. of combi bearing in each roller assembly.

clause.title: Bank Seat Beam (BSB) Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 16 for Bank Seat Beam (BSB). The function of the BSB is to support bridge and nose during launching operation. BSB also sustain the loads during launching and de-launching operation. These loads are transferred to the ground through BSB. BSB supports the sliding platform during launching of nose modules in cantilever mode, this is the pivot point to support launching system and transfer load to ground. BSB also avoid the toppling of launching vehicle and support the nose system while laying the bridge modules in simply supported condition at both ends.

The function of BSB is to support the sliding platform during the nose modules launch and to keep the nose modules in raised condition for avoiding structural interference during bridge modules launch. BSB comprises of a BSB cylinder and the two (2) guide tubes. BSB cylinder provides the necessary stroke for the BSB vertical structure assembly movement. Guide tubes are used to sustain transverse loads during the bridge launch. Refer Figure 6 for location of BSB.
One (1) BSB comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 9.

clause.title: BSB Cylinder
clause.para:
Refer Figure 18 and Figure 17 for BSB cylinder. BSB cylinder is used for adjusting the height of BSB during the launch of nose. BSB cylinder is actuated with PVG-2.
Two (2) hose (pressure line and return line) are connected from PVG and stowed on launching platform. QDC are provided for quick connection and start operations. BSB cylinder is lowered completely after launch of bridge, to make sure sufficient gap is created between bridge and nose modules such that no contact to be made during traffic movement. Oil flow from trolley based power pack to BSB cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 20.

clause.title: Turn Buckle
clause.para: Refer Figure 21 for turn buckle. Turnbuckle is used for fixing the BSB to base structure in launching condition and transportation condition. During launching operation, turn buckle is attached to nose and during transportation condition it is attached to BSB sliding member and BSB base. This is adjusted to achieve in simply supported mode. Levelled nose modules before start of bridge module launching. This levelled nose is critical to ensure smooth docking and locking of bridge modules. Spirit gauge is used to check the level of nose modules.

clause.title: BSB to Nose Locking Pin
clause.para: Refer Figure 23 and Figure 17 for BSB vertical structure to nose locking pin. Locking pin is used to lock BSB and NEM while launching operation with the help of bush and nut.

clause.title: Crank Lever Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 24 for crank lever assembly. Crank lever assembly is used to rotate the locking screw of locking screw assembly. The crank has square female head which fits into male head of locking screw. At the other end of crank lever assembly grip handle is provided to resist slippery motion during turning.

clause.title: Bridge Superstructure
clause.para: Refer Figure 25 for bridge superstructure. Bridge superstructure is mechanically launched single span mobile bridging system. The bridge is laid in varying lengths from 14 m to 46 m in steps of 6.5 m. It provides a 4 m wide roadway for traffic. The bridge is fully decked with anti-skid surface. Once the launching nose is deployed the bridge modules are assembled together over it. During bridge modules launching over nose assembly to avoid possible run-away of bridge modules bridge to nose locking pin is used.

Two (2) adjacent bridge modules are locked manually with bridge to bridge locking mechanism over nose modules while launching. Locking mechanism is provided at the diagonally opposite bottom corner of the bridge module side girder to maintain the interchangeability among the modules.

The bridge superstructure consists of bridge modules and ramps. Ramps provides smooth movement of the vehicles on and out of the bridging system. Refer Table 10 for bridge superstructure subassemblies.

clause.title: Bridge End Module (BEM) Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 25 and Figure 28 for Bridge End Module (BEM). The BEM construction is tapered at one end; the other end is similar to the BCM. The taper end is having the arrangement for end ramp resting. Ramp support structure is provided for ramp articulation. Butt male and female arrangement is provided on locking side of BEM to maintain the interchangeability of each bridge modules, refer Figure 27. There are total four (4) nos. of BEM in one (1) set of MB. For formation of any bridge span two (2) nos. of BEMs are required.

All BCMs are connected to each other with the help of locking mechanism between two (2) BEM. Locking mechanism provides locking of the already launched bridge modules to the launching nose to avoid possible ‘run-away’.

The BEM is provided with hinged flap assembly in the middle portion of the taper end. Flap will remain open during launching due to roller reaction during bridge pushing to allow proper sliding of the bridge modules over the launching nose and falls down automatically as soon as the bridge is pushed completely. BEM is provided with hooks for lifting bridge with the help of MHD. The arrangement of various components along with BEM is shown in Figure 28. One (1) BEM comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 11.

clause.title: Flap Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 29 and Figure 30 for flap assembly. Flap assembly is provided in the middle portion of the taper end. It supports the slider crank assembly, guide roller assembly and support roller assembly. It is held in horizontal portion using slider crank assembly. Guide roller and support roller are provided for smooth rolling on nose assembly during launching operation. Once the BEM’s are positioned on NEM’s on completion of launching all seven (7) bridge modules, the flap assembly to be lowered using BSB cylinder and flap assembly becomes in-plane with bridge surface. It also helps in engaging one end of the flap held in bridge pushing mechanism during bridge launching operation. Refer Figure 28 for location of flap assembly.

To operate hand pump, lever is provided on top deck which is articulate using handle and provision is given on top deck. One drain port is provided below the hand pump.

clause.para: Refer Figure 37 for bridge end support assembly. The bridge end support assembly rests on foot rest assembly of BEM. It transfers complete load of bridge structure and transporting vehicle to ground. Two (2) nos. of foot rest assemblies are mounted on bridge end support assembly. For location refer Figure 28.

Each BEM is having eight (8) nos. of curb assemblies. These curb assemblies are hinged with bridge module with the help of lock and pin. This curbs opens manually after bridge launching.

It is used for correct locking and to avoid misalignment during docking operation with adjacent bridge modules. Refer Figure 28 for location of male and female guide beak.

clause.title: Support Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 40 for support roller assembly. Support roller assembly helps to slide the bridge modules over nose modules during launching and de-launching operation, refer Figure 42. Rollers are fitted beneath the top deck of each bridge module. Each BEM is provided with two (2) nos. of sliding rollers. For location of support roller assembly refer Figure 28.

clause.title: Guide Roller Assembly
clause.para:
Refer Figure 41 for guide roller assembly. Guide rollers helps to avoid lateral movement and provide guidance to bridge modules while sliding on nose modules during launching and de-launching operation, refer Figure 42. Each BEM is provided with two (2) nos. of guide rollers. It is mounted below the top deck assembly of BEM refer

clause.title: Bridge to Bridge Locking Mechanism
clause.para: Refer Figure 43 for bridge to bridge locking mechanism. It is fitted on flat side of BEM, which is locked by adjacent bridge modules, for location refer Figure 28. When two (2) bridge modules are docked adjacent to each other they are locked using bridge to bridge locking mechanism and prevent separation during transmission of load. The locking mechanism experiences shear and tensile load during traffic passing on bridge. The link plate from adjacent bridge module, goes into the gap between bottom girder and locked in position by operating gearbox mechanism. Here, the horizontal movement of the hollow locking pin is achieved by the movement of nut over a threaded pin. A bevel pinion rotates the threaded pin, which is in mesh with a bevel gear. The bevel gear is manually rotated from top. The gearbox is operated by operator standing on top deck of bridge using hand wheel assembly.

clause.title: Link Plate
clause.para: Refer Figure 44 for link plate. Link plate is provided at locking side of BEM. Link plate is used to engage adjacent bridge modules. The link plate from adjacent bridge module, goes into the gap between bottom girder and are locked in position by operating screw nut mechanism.

clause.title: Ramp Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 45 for ramp roller assembly. Ramp roller assembly aids in guiding the ramp module to be properly placed over the bridge end modules and prevent transverse dislocation. Ramp roller assembly also aids in reducing the load impact on the ramp cylinder.

Butt male and female are welded on both sides of the BCM to maintain the interchangeability of each bridge modules, refer Figure 27. All BCM are connected to each other with the help of locking mechanism between two (2) BEM. ‘run-away’. Refer Figure 25 for location of BCM. Hooks are provided on BCM structure to lift BCM with the help of MHD. One (1) BCM comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 13.

These curb assemblies are hinged with bridge module with the help of lock and pin. This curbs opens manually after bridge launching.

clause.title: Guide Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 41 for guide roller assembly. Guide rollers helps to avoid lateral movement and provide guidance to bridge modules while sliding on nose modules during launching and de-launching operation, refer Figure 42. Each BCM is provided with four (4) nos. of guide rollers. It is mounted below the top deck assembly of BCM, refer Figure 46 for location of guide roller assembly.

clause.title: Bridge to Bridge Locking Mechanism
clause.para: Refer Figure 43 for bridge to bridge locking mechanism. Two (2) nos. of bridge to bridge locking mechanism are mounted diagonally on both the sides of BCM. When two (2) bridge modules are docked adjacent to each other they are locked with the help of locking mechanism and prevent separation during transmission of load. The locking mechanism experiences shear and tensile load during traffic passing on bridge. The link plate from adjacent bridge module, goes into the gap between bottom girder and locked in position by operating screw nut mechanism. Here, the horizontal movement of the hollow locking pin is achieved by the movement of nut over a threaded pin. A bevel pinion rotates the threaded pin, which is in mesh with a bevel gear. The bevel gear is manually rotated from top. The gearbox is operated by operator standing on top deck of bridge using hand wheel assembly. For location of locking mechanism on BCM refer Figure 46.

clause.title: Link Plate
clause.para: Refer Figure 44 for link plate. Link plate is provided at both side of BCM. Link plate is used to engage adjacent bridge modules. The link plate from adjacent bridge module, goes into the gap between bottom girder and are locked in position by operating screw nut mechanism.

clause.title: Ramp Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 48 for ramp assembly and for location refer Figure 26. Ramp assembly facilitate smooth entry and exit of passing vehicles on the bridge, refer Figure 50.

To lock ramp with BEM, ramp lock box assembly provided, refer Figure 49. To lock ramps launching and de-launching operation ramp lock arrangement is provided, which avoids the misalignment of ramp from BEM structure and RSS, refer Figure 51.

figure.title: Exit of Vehicle from Ramp Assembly

clause.title: Ramp Filler Panel Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 52 and Figure 53 for ramp filler panel assembly. Filler panels are provided for easy and smooth entry and exit of light weight vehicles on the bridge. It provides the additional passage for moving the light weight vehicle upto load class MLC-30.

clause.title: Hand Wheel Assembly
clause.para:
Refer Figure 54 for hand wheel. It is used to rotate the gear box of bridge to bridge locking mechanism to lock and unlock the bridge modules during launching and
de-launching operations. To rotate gear box using hand wheel assembly slot on top deck of bridge modules is given. Refer Figure 26 for hand wheel location on bridge.

clause.title: Bridge to Nose Locking Pin Assembly
clause.para: Bridge to Nose Locking Pin is used to lock the launched bridge module with the nose module beneath them. It makes sure that there is no relative dislocation between the launched bridge and nose modules till the next bridge module is launched, docked and locked with the adjacent bridge module. Refer Figure 55 for bridge to nose locking pin.

clause.title: Launching System
clause.para: The launching system is mounted on 10x10 HMV vehicles, refer Figure 57. The nose and bridge modules deployment is carried out with the help of launching system. The launching system consists of the following major subassemblies:

item.text: HMV 10x10 (Launching Vehicle)
Launching Mechanical System
Launching Hydraulic System
Launching Electrical / Electronic System
Material Handling Device (MHD)
Auxiliary Power Unit (APU)

clause.title: HMV 10x10 (Launching Vehicle)
clause.para:
Refer Figure 58 for HMV 10x10 (Launching Vehicle). HMV 10x10 is a Launching Vehicle (LV) used for high cross-country mobility. The whole launching system is mounted on this vehicle chassis by Cleat plate construction. No welding or drilling is allowed on vehicle chassis during integration of the structures. It has permanent 10x10 wheel drive engagable with all differentials locks provision. One set of MB contains
two (2) nos. of launching vehicles. Refer User Handbook of HMV 10x10 for more details.

clause.title: Launching Mechanical System
clause.para: The launching mechanical system is mounted on 10x10 vehicle platform. The mechanical system is fitted to the vehicle chassis by means of mounting studs. Launching system comprises of following subassemblies:

clause.title: Subframe Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 59 for subframe assembly. Subframe is a common platform, on which all the subsystems of launching system are fitted. Subframe is the main member, which transfers the load to the vehicle chassis.

Subframe assembly is a fabricated structure which is fastened on vehicle chassis with the aid of cleat plates. Transportation lock and launching lock are provided on subframe. Launching lock is towards crane side and transportation lock is towards cabin side, these lock are for connecting the subframe with sliding platform during transportation and launching operation, refer Figure 60. Screw rod assembly is provided at the rear end of the subframe. This assembly is used to connect the extension link with nose assembly during bridge launching operation.

clause.title: 2.4.2.1.1 Outrigger Extension Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 61 for outrigger extension assembly. Two (2) nos. of outriggers are configured of subframe. With these outriggers, stabilizers are attached. Stabilizer cylinders are connected to subframe assembly as shown in Figure 51. Two (2) stabilizer cylinders are on left side of vehicle and other two (2) are on right side.

Left side stabilizer cylinders are fixed to subframe structure. Right side stabilizer cylinders are connected to outrigger extension assembly which is extended during launching operation. In the launching sequence, the outriggers two (2 nos.) and stabilizers (4 nos.) are extended to level the launching system.

clause.title: 2.4.2.1.2 Rail Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 62 for rail assembly. Two (2) standard rails compatible (with sliding platform rollers) are welded on the skid structure inside which the sliding platform assembly with launching platform moves in forward and backward direction. The rails compatible with the sliding platform rollers, are welded at one side of subframe. The forces and moments during launching of nose are transferred to the structure through these rails.

clause.title: 2.4.2.1.3 Elephant Foot Assembly
clause.para: Refer figure for elephant foot assembly. It is mounted on both side subframe assembly during transportation with the help of wing nuts. Before starting system operation elephant foot assembly remove manually from subframe and engaged with ball and socket joint in bottom portion of each stabilizer cylinders. Ball and sockets are used to considerate the ground level conditions. Elephant foot assembly gives support to stabilizer cylinder and launching system. Due to elephant foots whole weight transfer to ground properly.

clause.title: Sliding Platform Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 64 for Sliding platform assembly. The sliding platform is fabricated structure from channels, boxes and plates.

figure.title: Sliding Platform Assembly in Launching System

clause.para: Launching platform and tilt cylinder are mounted on the sliding platform. Sliding platform is used to move the launching platform in forward and backward direction during bridge launching and de-launching operation. To assist sliding platform in moving rails of subframe, four (4) sets of double roller assemblies are provided. The sliding platform is pushed / pulled by sliding platform cylinder.
While launching the nose modules, BSB of home bank is attached to the sliding platform to get more resisting moment against toppling. Refer Table 15 for sliding platform subassemblies.

clause.title: 2.4.2.2.1 Sliding Platform Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 66 for sliding platform roller. Roller assembly takes the load during launching / de-launching operation. The sliding platform roller assembly, rolls inside the rails provided on the subframe assembly using combi roller bearings. Four (4) nos. of roller assemblies are fitted on the sliding platform structure. Each assembly is having one (1) roller mounting plate and two (2) nos. of combi bearing. With the help of roller assembly, sliding platform slide through the rail assembly of subframe structure, refer Figure 60.

clause.title: 2.4.2.2.2 Vertical Attachment Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 67 for vertical attachment assembly. Vertical attachment assembly is used for mounting the vertical attachment cylinder with sliding platform structure. Vertical attachment assembly helps to provide rigidity and transfer the load to BSB during nose module operation. Refer Figure 65 for location of vertical attachment assembly.

clause.title: 2.4.2.2.3 Horizontal Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 68 for horizontal roller assembly. Four (4) nos. of horizontal roller assemblies are fitted on the sliding platform structure. Sliding platform slide smoothly through the rail assembly of subframe structure with the help of horizontal roller assembly. Refer Figure 65 for location of horizontal roller assembly.

clause.title: Launching Platform Assembly
clause.para:
Refer Figure 69 for launching platform assembly. Nose modules are assembled and pushed / pulled on the launching platform assembly with the aid of nose pushing cylinder. Bridge modules pushed / pulled on the launched nose modules with the help of sliding platform assembly. The launching platform assembly is connected with sliding platform assembly through a hinge joint and tilt cylinder. Tilt cylinder provides + 4 deg. to - 24 deg. articulation to launching platform during launching and
de-launching operations at different bank slopes.
Refer Figure 70 for launching platform subassemblies. Launching platform assembly comprises of following subassemblies, refer Table 16.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.1 Nose Support Roller Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 71 for nose support roller assembly. It is used to support the nose modules during launching and de-launching operation for sliding over launch platform. It has a rectangular shape and rollers are mounted on each corner. It consists four (4) nos. of roller assembly which are mounted parallel to each other. Each roller assembly has two (2) nos. of rollers. Refer Figure 70 for location of support roller assembly.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.2 Bridge Pushing Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 72 for bridge pushing assembly. The purpose of the assembly is to engage and disengage the bridge modules during operation. Bridge pushing assembly is mounted in rear end of launching platform and operated by hook tilting cylinder to engage / disengage bridge modules during bridge operation. Refer Figure 70 for location of bridge pushing assembly.
Bridge module kept on nose assembly and this module are pushed / pulled with the help of sliding platform assembly. Slings are provided which are engaged with the hooks on bridge modules.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.3 Nose Support Rail Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 73 for nose support rail assembly. Nose support rail assembly arrangement is fitted at the front end of launching platform. The functional requirement of this arrangement is to support the nose module at the time of its placement on launching platform. It provides necessary articulation for alignment while docking with already placed nose modules with the help of nose levelling cylinder. It has provision of roller, which slides nose modules during operation.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.4 Friction Locking Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 74 for friction locking assembly. Friction locking assembly is fitted on the launching platform, refer Figure 70. Friction locking assembly is fixed with rubber pads for intermittent locking of the nose modules as and when required during the docking and undocking of the nose modules. It is used to lock already launched nose modules on launching platform. It unlocks the nose modules during push / pull operation of nose modules on launching platform. Two brake pads are actuated by a friction locking cylinder against the nose modules bottom chord. The friction force between the brake pads and the nose chords holds the nose modules during its launch.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.5 Nose Pushing Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 75 for nose pushing assembly. Nose pushing assembly fitted on catwalk side of the launching platform. It is used to engage / disengage nose pushing pin during nose operation on launching platform. Nose modules are pushed / pulled by nose pushing assembly with the help of nose pushing cylinder. Nose pushing assembly is attached with the cylinder rod end.

Nose pushing assembly bracket is operated through steel wire rope and handle assembly. The bracket holds the pushing pin of nose modules to push / pull the on launching platform. The pin will be released from bracket by operating the rope and pulley arrangement at the end of stroke. A roller assembly is connected with the pushing bracket and guided on channel to prevent the cylinder rod rotation and any movement. Refer Figure 70 for location of nose pushing assembly.

figure.title: Nose Pushing Assembly with Wire Rope

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.6 Nose Initial Push Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 77 for nose initial push assembly. The nose modules are pushed initially with the help of nose initial push assembly to lock with already placed nose modules. It is operated with the help of nose initial push cylinder. The pushing arrangement bracket gets engaged with the nose pushing pin and it is actuated by a nose levelling cylinder. Set of roller are connected to the pushing bracket at its bottom which guided inside the channel mounted on side of nose support frame. This roller prevents the bending due to eccentric load during nose pushing operation. Refer Figure 70 for location of push assembly.

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.7 Handle Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 79 for handle assembly. The handle assembly is connected to nose pushing assembly by means of wire rope. It is used to lock and unlock the nose pushing assembly during nose operation. Refer Figure 70 for location of handle assembly

clause.title: 2.4.2.3.8 Catwalk Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 70 and Figure 80 for location of catwalk assembly. Catwalk assembly provided for personnel movement on launching platform during nose operation. Total three (3) nos. of catwalk assemblies are mounted on launching platform.

There are total six (6) numbers of ratchet lashing belts are provided for holding the catwalk assembly in transportation condition. These belts are locked with welded lifting points provided on launching platform.

clause.title: Lifting Beam Assembly
clause.para: Lifting beam is used to connect MHD for lifting the nose and bridge modules during operation, refer Figure 81. With the help of lifting beam nose and bridge modules are lifted from CV and placed at designated location and vice versa. Slings are provided to handle bridge and nose modules. A hydraulic rotator is attached at the top of beam structure which is controlled by PVG mounted on crane for 360 deg. movement of lifting beam.

cell.text: Before operation connect the crane hoses with rotator.

clause.title: 2.4.2.4.1 Single Chain sling for Bridge
clause.para: Refer Figure 82 for single chain sling. This slings are attached to the lifting beam end corners. Single chain slings are used to lift the bridge modules from CV and place it over launched nose modules during operation and vice versa.

clause.title: 2.4.2.4.2 Double Chain Sling for Nose
clause.para: Refer Figure 83 for double chain sling. Double chain slings are used to lift the nose modules from CV and place it over launching platform during operation and vice versa.

clause.title: 2.4.2.4.3 Double Chain Sling for Nose (46m Assembly)
clause.para: Refer Figure 84 for double chain sling. This is fitted at the centre of lifting beam assembly. Double chain sling are used for lifting the NEM from launching platform to align it correctly and rest over to BSB and vice versa.

figure.title: Lifting Nose System with Double Chain Sling

clause.title: Ladder Assembly
clause.para: Refer Figure 85 for ladder assembly. Ladder assembly is kept below APU during transportation. Ladder is used to climb on launching system for person / operator / crew.

clause.title: BSB Extension Assembly

figure.title: BSB Extension Assembly in Launching Condition

clause.para: Refer Figure 86 and Figure 87 for BSB extension assembly. BSB extension assembly is used to increase the height of BSB during launching operation at home bank as per home bank ground condition. BSB extension assembly is fixed with vertical attachment during launching / de-launching as per BSB position. Whenever the stroke of vertical attachment cylinder is extracted and there is gap to connect with BSB, to overcome the gap BSB extension assembly is used.

clause.title: Launching Hydraulic System
clause.para: The hydraulic system of MB is used to operate the launching system for laying / retrieval of the bridge. The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPP) generates required hydraulic pressure for transmitting the power through oil flow to hydraulic cylinders. The hydraulic system mainly consists of following subsystems:

item.text: Hydraulic Reservoir
Pump with Drive Unit
Control Valves
Hydraulic Cylinders
Filters
Gauges and Accessories
Pipe and Hoses

clause.title: Hydraulic Reservoir
clause.para: Refer Figure 89 for location of reservoir on launching system. Hydraulic reservoir contains the hydraulic fluid for energy transfer. Reservoir has capacity of 750 litres. At the top of reservoir, a pressure gauge is provided which continuously monitors the pressure. A temperature sensor shows temperature on its display.

Reservoir supplies oil to both hydraulic pumps (main pump unit and auxiliary pump unit). Whenever the system runs on main pump unit, the valves of PTO line (launching, crane and oil cooler) to be open and valves of APU line are closed. Similarly, whenever the system runs on auxiliary pump unit the valves of APU line (launching, crane and oil cooler) to be open and valves of PTO line are closed.

During the replenishing of oil, the used oil is drained out by opening drain valve. Two manholes are provided for cleaning the reservoir from inside. Hydraulic reservoir has following accessories are fitted: (Refer Figure 90, Figure 91 and Figure 92):

item.text: Oil level indicator
Manifold block
4/2 DCV
Butterfly valves
Drain valve
Electronic temperature switch
Pressure gauge
Return line filter
Pressure relief valve
Pressure line filter
Oil level switch (float switch)
Offline filtration pump
Electric motor for offline filtration
Desiccant type air breather
Offline filter
Temp sensor

clause.title: Pump with Drive Unit
clause.para: Two (2) sets (Main pump unit (PTO) and Auxiliary pump unit (APU)) of pump are used to run hydraulic system. Each pump unit consist of two (2) identical pumps giving hydraulic oil to launching system and MHD separately.

clause.title: 2.4.3.2.1 Main Pump Unit
clause.para: Refer Figure 93 for main pump unit. This is a positive variable displacement load sensing pump is used to supply hydraulic oil to all cylinders during operation. Output capacity displacement 92 cc/rev and maximum pressure 420 bar. Main pump unit is being driven by PTO of the vehicle.

clause.title: 2.4.3.2.2 Auxiliary Pump Unit
clause.para:
Refer Figure 94 for auxiliary pump. The pump is specified as axial piston, variable displacement load sensing pump, displacement 92 cc/rev and maximum pressure
420 bar. On failure of main pump unit / PTO, auxiliary pump unit is used for system operation. Auxiliary pump unit is driven by APU and it has the same capacity of the main pump unit in terms of flow and pressure rating. All operations can be carried out with this unit.

clause.title: Control Valves
clause.para: Control valves are used for controlling the system operation. Following control valves are used for system operation.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.1 Check-Q-Meter
clause.para: Refer Figure 95, for the Check-Q-Meter fitted on tilt cylinder. The tilt cylinder, sliding platform cylinder, vertical attachment cylinder is provided with a Check-Q-Meter in the rod side and cap side to prevent run-away condition during bridge lowering. Since the loads are quite high on cylinder Check-Q-Meter has been preferred in tilt cylinder over counterbalance valve / over centre valve. Six (6) nos. of Check-Q-Meters are fitted in system.
Refer Table 17 for the location and qty. of Check-Q-Meter.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.2 Proportional Valve Group-1 (PVG-1)
clause.para: Refer Figure 97 for Proportional Valve Group-1 (PVG-1). PVG-1 contains PVG-32 valve bank. PVG-32 is a combination of directional and flow control valve. PVG-1 with seven (7) bank proportional valve is used to operate two (2) outrigger and four (4) stabilization cylinder during levelling operation. It is mounted on the subframe of launching system.

cell.text: PVG valve has to be undergo overhauling after completely 10 years or 500 launching cycles of system whichever is earlier. It is recommended overhauling to be carried out at OEM premises or in presence of OEM representative suitably.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.3 Proportional Valve Group-2 (PVG-2)
clause.para: Refer Figure 98 and Figure 99 for Proportional Valve Group-2 (PVG-2). PVG-2 contains two (2) valve banks. PVG-120 and PVG-32. PVG-2 is a combination of directional and flow control valve. It is mounted on launching platform. Eleven (11) bank proportional valve is used to operate following cylinders during launching and de-launching operations.

item.text: BSB Cylinder
Hook Tilting Cylinder
Friction Locking Cylinder
Vertical Attachment Cylinder
Tilt Cylinder (Nose Lowering)
Tilt Cylinder (Bridge Launching)
Nose Levelling Cylinder
Nose Initial Pushing Cylinder
Sliding Platform Cylinder
Nose Pushing Cylinder

cell.text: PVG valve has to be undergo overhauling after completely 10 years or 500 launching cycles of system whichever is earlier. It is recommended overhauling to be carried out at OEM premises or in presence of OEM representative suitably.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.4 4/2 Direction Control Valve
clause.para: Refer Figure 100 for 4/2 Direction Control Valve (DCV). DCV allows the oil to flow into different paths, it controls the start, stop and direction of flow. It is mounted on hydraulic reservoir to control the oil flow, refer Figure 90 and Figure 100 for location of 4/2 DCV. DCV with manual over ride has been used for operating all the outriggers. Provision is made for independent operations of all outriggers for levelling of the platform before launching. After levelling of system, it directs the flow to launching operations.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.5 Pilot Operated Check valve
clause.para: Pilot operated check valve allows the forward as well as reverse flow with the help of external pilot pressure signal. It is mounted on both BEM to interchange connection between ramp cylinder and BSB cylinder.

figure.title: Pilot Operated Check Valve of BEM

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.6 Pressure Relief Valve
clause.para: Refer Figure 102 for pressure relief valve. A pressure relief valve is a type of safety valve used to control or limit the pressure in a system. It is mounted on hydraulic reservoir, refer Figure 91 for location of valve. It is used in the offline filtration unit.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.7 Butterfly Valve
clause.para: Refer Figure 103 for butterfly valve. Butterfly valve are used for regulating the flow of oil in reservoir. It is operated in a quarter-turn rotational motion to control the flow of oil. It is mounted on the hydraulic reservoir to control oil flow of PTO and APU pump, refer Figure 90 for location of valve. Total four (4) nos. of butterfly valves are fitted on reservoir. It is a rotary valve provide with lever for ON / OFF function.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.8 Flow Control Valve
clause.para: Flow control valve controls the flow by adjusting the cross-section. Two (2) nos. of flow control valve are fitted on reservoir behind to pressure gauge, refer Figure 104.

clause.title: 2.4.3.3.9 Drain Valve
clause.para: Refer Figure 90 and Figure 105 for drain valve. Drain valve is used to drain the oil from reservoir during maintenance activity. It is a rotary valve provide with lever for ON / OFF function. It is mounted on hydraulic reservoir bottom.

cell.text: If the NAS level is found higher than seven (7), switch on offline filtration system until NAS level is upto seven (7). If still NAS level is higher than seven (7) then oil is contaminated and it has to be drain from reservoir using drain valve.

clause.title: Hydraulic Cylinders
clause.para: Refer Figure 106 and Figure 107 for the hydraulic cylinders. The MB system is operated using 12 Types of linear double acting hydraulic cylinder. The following are the functions of the cylinder:

cell.text: To hold the single nose module during launching operation push / pull nose module
To level the nose module during launching
To lock nose module on launching platform
To engage bridge pushing assembly and hold bridge modules
To slide the sliding platform and push / pull bridge modules on launched nose
To connect the sliding platform to BSB
To level the bank seat beam support
The Qty. of cylinders mentioned in above table, is for one (1) launching system.

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.1 Outrigger Extension Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 108 for outrigger extension cylinder. To extent stabilizer cylinder at required position outrigger extension cylinders are used. Two (2) nos. of outrigger cylinder are provided on front and rear right side of launching system. Outrigger extension cylinders are fixed on the subframe which extends right side stabilizer cylinders only for location refer Figure 106. Before operating the outrigger cylinder, the front outrigger cylinder is to be activated to increase the width of the support. The outrigger extension cylinder is operated PVG-1. The extension cylinders are to be activated through electrically operated direction control valves and hence the control rotary. Oil flow from reservoir to outrigger cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 109.

cell.text: Make sure during launching operation outrigger extension cylinder to be operate before stabilizer cylinder.

figure.title: Outrigger Extension Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.2 Stabilizer Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 110 for stabilizer cylinder. To level the launching system stabilizer cylinders are used. Stabilizer cylinder transfers the weight of launching system to ground. Elephant foot assembly are provided to stabilizer cylinder for high soil bearing capacity and increased load transfer area. Due to elephant foot assembly whole weight transfer to ground properly. Elephant foot are fitted at the end of stabilizer cylinder with ball and socket joints. Ball and sockets are used to considerate the ground level conditions. Total four (4) nos. of elephant foot rests and stabilizer cylinders are provided in launching system. For location of stabilizer cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to stabilizer cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 111.

figure.title: Stabilizer Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.3 Tilt Cylinder
clause.para:
Refer Figure 112 for tilt cylinder. Tilt cylinder is fitted on the rear side of the launching platform. Its function is to tilt the launching platform from + 4 deg. to – 24 deg. It is also used to tilt the bridge pushing bracket which facilitates the easy engagement and disengagement of hook with the bridge module. For location of tilt cylinder refer
Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to tilting cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 113.

figure.title: Tilt Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.4 Nose Pushing Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 114 for nose pushing cylinder. The nose modules are moved forward / backward by nose pushing cylinder on launching platform. Nose modules placed on launching platform are pushed / pulled by nose pushing cylinder. For location of nose pushing cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to nose pushing cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 115.

figure.title: Nose Pushing Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.5 Nose Initial Pushing Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 116 for nose initial pushing cylinder. Nose initial pushing cylinder is used for pushing the single nose assembly after placing on launching platform. The nose modules are placed on the launching platform by the handling device, and it is pushed towards the far bank by means of nose initial pushing cylinders equipped with the pushing mechanisms. Nose initial pushing bracket is also attached at the rod end of cylinder. During retrieval, the bracket of the mechanism is reversed so as to pull the nose modules towards the home bank. For location of nose initial pushing cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to nose initial pushing cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 117.

cell.text: If rubbing noise observed during extension of nose pushing cylinder under no load condition, same to be neglected since this is normal phenomenon for pilot operated check valve operation being operated at high flow rate.

figure.title: Nose Initial Push Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.6 Nose Levelling Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 118 for nose levelling cylinder. The nose levelling cylinder is used to level the nose module on the launching platform with the other placed nose module so that locking of the two (2) noses is done easily. For location of nose levelling cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to nose levelling cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 119.

figure.title: Nose Levelling Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.7 Friction Locking Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 120 for friction locking cylinder. The friction locking cylinder is used in friction locking assembly for intermittent locking of the nose modules as and when required during the docking and undocking of the nose modules.

When the nose modules are placed on the launching platform, it is over hanging on the rear side of the launching platform. Some additional support is required to prevent the nose modules from falling down on the rear side of the sliding platform. For location of friction locking cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to friction locking cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 121.

figure.title: Friction Locking Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.8 Hook Tilting Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 122 for hook tilting cylinder. Bridge modules are placed over the launched nose modules to launch over it, there must be some sliding mechanism to move it towards the far bank. The purpose of the hook tilting cylinder is to engage and disengage the bridge pushing bracket with the bridge modules during operation. It is placed rear side of the launching platform. For location of hook tilting cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to hook tilting cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 123.

figure.title: Hook Tilting Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.9 Sliding Platform Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 124 for sliding platform cylinder. It is used to operate the sliding platform. The sliding platform is mounted on the rails provided on the subframe assembly using bearing rollers. It is moved back and forth by a sliding cylinder, one end of which is fitted with the front end of the sliding platform. For location of sliding platform refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to sliding platform cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 125.

figure.title: Sliding Platform Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.10 Vertical Attachment Cylinder
clause.para: Refer Figure 126 for vertical attachment cylinder. The cylinder assists the sliding platform to transfer the load to BSB to increase the resisting toppling movement during the launch of nose assembly in cantilever mode. For location of vertical attachment cylinder refer Figure 106. Oil flow from reservoir to vertical attachment cylinder reference block diagram shown in Figure 127.

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.11 Ramp Cylinder
clause.para: Refer section 2.3.1.3 for ramp cylinder details.

clause.title: 2.4.3.4.12 BSB Cylinder
clause.para: Refer section 2.2.3.1 for BSB cylinder details.

figure.title: Vertical Attachment Cylinder Hydraulic Oil Flow Block Diagram

clause.title: 2.4.3.5.1 Pressure Line Filter
clause.para: Refer Figure 128 for pressure line filter. Pressure line filter is use to filter the oil of pressure line. It is mounted on hydraulic reservoir, refer Figure 91 and Figure 128 for location pressure line filter. Filtration rating is upto 5 microns with nominal operating pressure of 420 bar. It has provision of clogging indicator. When clogging indicator indicates, replace the filter element.

clause.title: 2.4.3.5.2 Return Line Filter
clause.para: Refer Figure 129 for return line filter. Return line filters the oil before flowing back to the hydraulic reservoir. This helps in keeping the reservoir clean by removing all the dirt particles and enhance the operating efficiency. It is mounted on hydraulic reservoir, refer Figure 90 and Figure 129 for location of filter. Its nominal operating pressure is upto 25 bar with filtration rating upto 10 microns. It has provision of clogging indicator. When clogging indicator indicates, replace the filter element.

clause.title: 2.4.3.5.3 Offline Filtration Unit
clause.para: Refer Figure 130 for offline filtration unit. It maintains desired level of cleanliness in hydraulic reservoir. clause.title: Bridging Operations
clause.para: To form 46 m MB, system is transported by one (1) no. off HMV 10x10 LV and five (5) nos. off HMV 8x8 CVs and launched across the gap by launching system. It covers the following actions:

item.text: Evaluation of the site for laying of the bridge and the home and far bank side soil condition.
Selection of routes in and out for the bridge carrying vehicles and finalizing the alignment for the launching of the bridge.
Preparatory work of marking at the bridge site for levelling off the ground, clearance of the area, the approaches and abutment.

Preparatory work on the bridging vehicle and the vehicle waiting areas in the terms of the bridge configuration, accessories to be brought forward, the expedients required for vehicle movement up to bridge line / abutment.

clause.title: Evaluation of Bridge Site
clause.para: The commander of the system operations is required to visit and evaluate the options available to him for launching the bridge across the gap / trench identified. Make sure the soil bearing capacity is within permissible limit also adequate for the deployment of the equipment. The evaluation must bring out the limitations or compulsions imposed by the site, e.g. slopes, parking areas, bearing capacity, depth of gap / trench, water level, water current, width of the gap and visibility. It must also bring out the tasks required in the preparatory stages, and the resources required to perform these tasks.

clause.title: Preparatory Work of Bridge Site
clause.para: After new site is selected and found suitable, site preparation is required. This involves clearing and preparation of approach way, deciding the bridge abutment line, marking the central line on the home bank as well as far bank, vehicle alignment marker lines and vehicle positioning line. Markers on home and far banks are also placed for correct deployment of the bridge along the central line.

clause.title: Do’s and Don’ts of the System

item.text: Adjust the BSB position manually such that it is placed exactly below the vertical attachment of the sliding platform assembly.
Make sure that all switches of joystick console are working properly.
Before start of the launching operation, make sure that position of the sliding member of the BSB is in expanded condition.
Before operating the sliding platform, make sure rail assembly of the subframe is completely clean.
Check the power LED is glowing on JC before operation of joystick console.
Pressure reading is to be confirm during launching operating (launching pressure for crane 300 bar and launching system is 240 bar).
Make sure the transportation lock is removed before operating the sliding platform assembly.
Keep the mode of operation of selector switch on remote mode when operating through JC.
Before start of the launching operation, make sure that there is no leakage in any hydraulic assembly.
Make sure the friction lock is engaged with nose module assembly before docking another nose module.
Before pushing the nose assembly, make sure the nose pushing bracket is properly engaged with nose pushing pin.
Adjust the nose levelling platform slightly for proper docking and locking of the nose modules.
Before starting the nose and bridge modules lifting operation from MHD, make sure the CV containing nose and bridge modules are in prescribe positioned.
Make sure the mounting surface of the BSB is adequately horizontal using spirit level before start of launching operation.
Make sure lock plates of the all pin are intact in their position and tighten correctly.
Before putting the first NEM make sure launching platform is tilted to 4 deg. in upward condition.
At the time of retracting the launching platform assembly for lowering the nose assembly at home bank, ensure nose assembly is properly held up by crane.
Maintain the gap of 2700 mm between home bank side BSB centre to end of the subframe.
For docking the bridge modules, adjustment in up and down direction is to be carried out in bridge module which is being docked.
After launching the bridge assembly, home bank side BSB is to be lower first and after that far bank side is to be lowered.
Before operating the hand pump in far bank side, make sure hand pump is filled with oil.
Before placing filler panel assembly, make sure that nose extension assembly is completely lowered from its launching condition.

For de-launching operation, make sure centre line of the bridge pushing mechanism is completely aligned with centreline of the launched bridge assembly (after outriggers expanding). Use rear view camera for aligning the centre line.
Make sure sufficient gap is available between bottoms of the ramp and top of the RSS.
Gird heater switch must be attempted for 10 sec. when environmental temperature reaches below -20 0C.
Do not move the launching vehicle if launching platform assembly is in launching condition.
Do not start the launching operation if longitudinal and transvers axis of the launching vehicle is not properly levelled.
If two (2) nose modules are not properly aligned, don’t try to assemble it forcefully.
Do not operate the nose initial pushing cylinder further if two (2) nose modules are completely locked and docked.
Do not operate the nose pushing cylinder if friction lock is engaged.
Do not keep lifting hook of the nose module in lifted condition after placed on launching platform. It may interfere with bridge assembly during launching.
Do not operate the system if there is vibration in the nose assembly at the time of lowering at far bank.
Do not start the bridge launching operation, if bridge pushing mechanism is not correctly aligned with centre of bridge modules.
Do not operate the sliding platform cylinder further than its available stroke.
Do not push bridge modules further, if two (2) bridge modules are docked and locked.
Do not try to forcefully align two modules while launching operation.
If bridge to bridge locking pin is engaged, do not operate the sliding platform cylinder further.

If butt male and butt female of the bridge modules are engaged and male female jaw plates are not engaged, do not push jaw plates further, adjust the bridge module which is docked in up and down direction.
If tilting is observed after docking three (3) bridge modules, do not continue the launching, level the top face of the nose assembly by tightening the turn buckles.
Do not operate APU with normal starting procedure when environmental temperature reaches below -20 0C.

Make sure that nobody is below the lifted bridge modules in launching operation.

clause.title: Pre-operating Checks Before Starting De-launching Operation
clause.para: Pre-operating checks before de-launching operation are as follows:

item.text: Make sure the positions of hydraulic valves are as per Table 37.
Make sure centreline of the bridge pushing mechanism is completely aligned with centreline of the launched bridge assembly (after outriggers expanding).
Make sure that bridge to nose locking pin is removed before pulling the bridge assembly.
Make sure sufficient gap is available between vehicle and ramp assembly.

clause.title: Operating Sequence
clause.para: There are six (6) major operating stages which are followed sequentially:

item.text: PTO engage and disengage procedure
Levelling of launching vehicle
Nose launching operation
Bridge launching operation
Bridge retrieval operation
Nose retrieval operation
PTO Engage
Start the vehicle.

Air pressure to be maintained up to 8 bar. Monitor the air pressure on front air pressure gauge, which is installed on LV instrument panel, as shown in
Figure 169.
Turn ON PTO switch to engage PTO.
Press the PTO cruise set increment switch to increase the rpm of PTO up to 1300 rpm to 1500 rpm.
PTO Disengage
Press the rpm switch to decrease the rpm of PTO, refer Figure 171.
Turn OFF PTO switch to disengage PTO, refer Figure 170.
Refer section 2.3.3 for pre-operating checks before launching.
Mark the area of 25 m x 25 m for LV placement, Refer Figure 172
Park the 10x10 LV in the revers mode at 4.4 m away from home bank edge as shown in Figure 173.

Make sure butterfly valves on reservoir are in open condition, refer
Figure 174.

figure.title: Butterfly Valves are in Open Condition

item.text: Engage the PTO as per procedure mentioned in section 2.4.1 to hydraulic pump or start APU engine.
Lift the ladder from its transportation position and fix it near the crane side of the launching vehicle next to the PDU as shown in Figure 175.

figure.title: Ladder in Position on Launching System

item.text: Climb on launcher by using ladder for opening of the door of PDU and MDP.
Select the power input through ‘BATTERY SELECTOR’ switch form PDU, refer Figure 176.
Turn ON the POWER ON / OFF SELECTOR switch to power ON the PDU, refer Figure 177.
Switch on the air oil cooler knob located in PDU, refer Figure 178.

Turn on lights switch knob located in PDU during night operation, refer
Figure 179.
Switch-ON the selector switch to power ON the MDP, as shown in Figure 180.
Energize direction control valve (DCV-1) through selector switch on MDP to ‘P/F LVL’ for operation of PVG-1 of outrigger system, refer Figure 181.

figure.title: Mode of Operation Selector Switch on MDP

item.text: Select the PTO and APU load sensing line provided on the reservoir. Select the Load Sensing Line provided on reservoir to OTR/LAUNCH operation mode by operating ball valves, refer Figure 182.

Extend both outrigger cylinders by using PVG-1, refer Figure 183 and
Figure 184. Extend the Outrigger fully till its maximum stroke.
Lift the elephant foot assembly from its transportation position and engage with ball joint in bottom portion of the stabilizer cylinders, refer Figure 185.
Extend all the stabilizer cylinders using PVG-1 till it touches the ground, as show in Figure 186.

The stabilizer cylinders are extended to relieve the wheels from vehicle load. The launching vehicle is levelled in lateral and longitudinal direction with respect to ground level using inclinometer mounted on sub frame assembly. The level of the platform is displayed on the MDP, as shown in Figure 187. (Levelling accuracy is +/- 1 deg.)

cell.text: The levelling accuracy must be +/- 1 degree.

item.text: Open the ratchet lashing belts of BSB and ratchet lashing belts which connect the LP and SP together.
Open the catwalk assembly of launching platform by removing hooks of ratchet lashing belts from welded lifting points, refer Figure 188 and Figure 189.
Operate selector switch on MDP from ‘P/F LVL’ to ‘LAUNCH OPRTN’ for operation of PVG-2 of launching mechanism. Refer Figure 181 for mode of operation selector switch on MDP.
Disengage the transportation lock of sliding platform located towards the cabin side, refer Figure 190.
Connect cable of the Launcher Joystick to MDP for operation of launcher through joystick.
Bring the sliding platform form transportation mode to launching mode. Lower the BSB and position it under vertical cylinder attachment and lock it, as per Figure 191.
Fix the mechanical lock of the sliding platform by operating the locking handle in subframe.
Extend the tilt cylinder by operating PVG-2 and tilt launch platform by 4 deg.
If required, adjust the BSB position manually such that it is placed exactly below the vertical attachment of the sliding platform.
Extend the vertical cylinder of sliding platform by operating PVG-2.

cell.text: If required attach 'BSB Extension' to the vertical attachment assembly of sliding platform as per gap available in site location. Make sure pressure on the vertical attachment cylinder is in between 40 bar to 50 bar.

item.text: Bring the Material Handling Device (MHD) from transportation mode to operating mode (Unfold).
Refer section 2.3.4 for pre-operating checks before launching.

Remove the ratchet lashing belts of the CV-1, refer Figure 192. Keep them in the CV-1 toolbox

Operate the MHD and attach the rotator of lifting beam. Simultaneously, connect the rotator hoses through QDC's. Connect all slings to lifting beam provided in CV-1 tool box, refer Figure 193 and Figure 194.

Attach the slings of lifting beam to NEM-1 which has pre attached BSB from the CV-1 as per lifting arrangement. Lift NEM-1 and place on the launching platform in such a way that one set of front roller of launching platform is completely inside the rails.

Make sure NEM-1 is locked by engaging nose pushing bracket to push pin of nose modules. Engage the friction locking pads to NEM-1 by extending the friction locking cylinder through PVG 2, refer Figure 196.
Remove slings from NEM-1 and attach the sling to NCM-1. Retract the friction lock cylinder and bring NEM 1 to its docking position.

Make sure that the push pin of NCM-1 towards the launching end lies in front of sliding plate of nose initial push assembly to avoid the backward slip of the NCM from the LP as shown in Figure 198.

Engage the friction locking pads to NCM-1. Relieve the nose pushing bracket of the nose pushing assembly from holding position (Release the holding position of nose pushing pin from nose pushing assembly).
Retract the nose pushing cylinder until the pushing bracket holds the next pushing pin and operate the nose pushing cylinder up to the defined position.

Remove the CV-1 and bring the CV-2 to the right hand side at approximate gap of 1 m between the centre of elephant foot rest and the side of the carrier vehicle platform. Remove the ratchet lashing belts of the CV-2.

Lift NEM-2 from the CV-2 with the help of MHD and place it in such way that one pair of roller is to be on the rear side of launching platform and the other pair of roller on extended launching platform.

Make sure that the push pin of NEM-2 towards the launching end lies in front of sliding plate of nose initial push assembly to avoid the backward slip of the module from the LP as shown in Figure 198.

Remove slings from the NEM-2. Operate the nose initial pushing cylinder and bring it to docking position. Operate the nose levelling cylinder in order to align the hole axis of nose jaws, if required.

Arrange the chain sling's on lifting beam as per nose assembly. Attach the slings at the center of the lifting beam to the NEM-2. Hold the complete nose module assembly with the help of MHD.

cell.text: Engage the friction lock with NEM-2, engage the nose pushing bracket with nose pushing pin, make sure lifting beam sling is connected to NEM-2.

item.text: Retract the tilt cylinder by operating PVG-2 to tilt the launching platform such that the launching nose assembly with BSB touches the ground of the far bank. Make sure that the end rollers of NEM-2 are free from load and are in released condition.

figure.title: BSB Touches the Ground at Far Bank

item.text: If applicable, remove pin connecting BSB extension assembly or vertical attachment cylinder with the BSB and take the vertical attachment upward.

Release the lock between the sliding platform and sub frame. Retract the sliding platform cylinder to full closed length and simultaneously operate the tilt cylinder to hang the launching nose assembly smoothly.

Attach the BSB to the bridge pushing hook with the help of slings and tilt the launching platform so that the home BSB is lifted from the ground. Fine-tune the position of BSB manually to align it with the nose module.

Lower the nose assembly by the MHD and attach it with the home BSB using BSB to nose locking pin. Align nose extension assembly wrt. sliding platform rails by adjusting the position of launching nose using MHD.
Attach the screw rod fitted on subframe to nose extension assembly by using the locking pin. Make sure the positioning of the screw rod assembly is at the center of nose extension assembly.
Remove the chain slings from the NEM-2.

Detach the turn buckles from BSB base structure and attach BSB to NEM-1 lifting hook. Tighten the turn buckles. Make the launching nose level approximately horizontal. The same can be verified using sprit level.
One (1) person walks over the launched nose towards the far bank and make sure the level of top face of the nose is horizontal by using spirit level.
Attach the turn buckle of BSB to far bank NEM-2. Tighten the turn buckles.
The launching nose assembly is now ready for launching of bridge modules.
Refer section 2.3.4 for pre operating checks before launching. Change the Selector Switch on the Joystick from Nose to Bridge.
Make sure that the rear side catwalk is in folded condition during entire bridge launching operation.
Before starting of bridge launching, bridge pulling / pushing slings and D shackle need to be fitted on hook tilting assembly for pulling/ pushing the bridge while launching.
Attach the slings and lift the BEM-1. Place the BEM-1 on launching nose such that flap is facing towards far bank and all the rollers of the bridge module rests on the launching nose.
Hold the one end of the BEM-1 in bridge pushing hook. Attach the chain slings connecting the BEM-1 to the bridge pushing assembly.

Remove the chain slings of the lifting beam from the BEM-1. Attach the slings to first ramp assembly on the CV-2. Place the ramp assembly on the RSS and lock it. Also locked ramp and RSS with ramp lock arrangement. Repeat this step for the second ramp also. Remove the chain slings attached to the ramp assembly.
Push the BEM-1 over the nose modules by extending the sliding platform cylinder till the pin hole of both the BEM-1 and NEM-2 are aligned.

cell.text: While pushing the bridge towards far bank make sure that the bridge pushing chain must be at the same level of the bridge (i.e. in horizontal position, no lifting of the chain).

Insert the bridge locking pin to lock the BEM-1 with the NEM-2, refer
Figure 212.
Remove the slings connecting the BEM-1 and bridge pushing assembly (launching platform). Retract the sliding platform cylinder for placing the next bridge module.

Insert the bridge locking pin in BCM-1 to lock the bridge assembly with the NEM as done earlier. Remove the slings connecting the BCM-1 and bridge pushing assembly. Retract the sliding platform cylinder for placing the next bridge module.

Remove the chain slings of lifting beam. Attach the chain slings connecting the hook at flap end of BEM-2 to the bridge pushing assembly.
