cell.text: Operate the tilt cylinder for aligning the bridge to bridge locking pin with respective holes. Visually make sure that both the pins have projected out from the jaw face.

item.text: Remove the bridge to nose locking pin. Push this assembly towards the far bank to the necessary position by extending the sliding platform cylinder.
Insert the bridge locking pin to lock the BEM-2 with the NEM as done earlier.
Remove the nose extension assembly connected to the LV screw rod on the home bank.
Change the mode of bridge end assembly from transportation mode to launched mode at both sides of the bridge using lever handle provided on the BEM and lock it using its locking pin.
Lift the mobile power pack located on CV-5 and place it over the bridge. Drive the mobile power pack trolley to the far bank from over the bridge.

Connect the hydraulic hoses located on mobile power pack trolley to BSB on far bank (Make sure P line and T line are connected correctly). Turn on the mobile power pack trolley engine by using recoil starter.

Remove the pins of BSB for lowering it. Lower the BSB of far bank side by actuating the lever in the (Directional Control Valve) DCV of BSB cylinder. Lock the BSB assembly by installing the pins in the slot provided.
Turn OFF the mobile power pack engine after use and remove the hoses.

cell.text: Make sure the bridge module is completely resting on the bridge end assembly and gap exists between nose and bridge support rollers.

item.text: Connect the hydraulic hoses of launching system to the BSB on home side (Make sure P line and T line are connected correctly) and operate the BSB using PVG-2.
Remove the pins of BSB for lowering it. Lower the BSB of home bank side. Lock the BSB assembly by installing the pins in the slot provided.

cell.text: Make sure the bridge module is completely resting on the bridge end assembly and gap exists between nose and bridge support rollers.

item.text: Connect the hydraulic hoses located on mobile power pack trolley to the connections present on BEM-1 at far end (Make sure P line and T line are connected correctly).
Turn on the mobile power pack trolley engine by using recoil starter.
Switch the lever on BEM-1 to ramp down condition. Operate the far bank ramp cylinder by actuating the lever of mobile power pack trolley to lower the end ramps.
Turn OFF the mobile power pack engine after use and remove the hoses.

cell.text: In absence or malfunction in mobile power pack trolley, hand pump present on the BEM can be used to lower the ramps. (Refer Figure 226)

item.text: Retract the launching platform and sliding platform assembly to its initial position. Lift the Stabilizer cylinder in upward direction. Move the LV in forward direction by approx. 8 m. Again level the launching system as per section 2.4.2.
Remove the locking pin of RSS and lower the RSS of BEM-2 at home bank manually.

cell.text: Do not touch ramp cylinder during RSS lowering, it may cause injury.

item.text: Attach the chain slings to the first ramp assembly on the CV-5. Place the ramp assembly on the RSS such way, other end of ramp touches the ground. Lock the ramp with RSS. Repeat this step for the second ramp also.

figure.title: Launching of Ramp at Home Bank

item.text: Remove the chain slings attached to the ramp assembly. Detach the lifting beam assembly from MHD and place lifting beam assembly on CV-5.
For the passing of light weight vehicles filler panels to be used to fill the gap between ramps.
Remove the nose extension assembly at home side for assembly of filler panels.

Open all curb assemblies of the launched bridge modules. Disengage PTO. Move LV from launching condition to transportation condition. Move the launching vehicle from home bank. Now, bridge is ready for the traffic.

clause.title: Operation of De-launching Bridge and Nose Modules

item.text: Refer section 2.3.5 for pre operating checks before de-launching.

cell.text: If the ramp filler panels are placed during launching operation, then remove filler panels manually and transport them to the home bank in manually handheld position over the launched bridge.

item.text: Drive the mobile power pack trolley to the far bank end over the launched bridge. Connect the hoses of mobile power pack trolley to BEM-1. Change the lever position of BEM to RAMP UP position.

Turn ON the mobile power pack engine manually using the recoil starter. Raise the ramps to its maximum cylinder stroke on the far bank by operating the lever on mobile power pack trolley. Turn OFF the mobile power pack engine after use and remove hoses.
Connect the hoses of mobile power pack trolley to BSB of far bank. Turn ON the mobile power pack engine manually using the recoil starter.

Remove the locking pins of BSB for starting the BSB raising operation. Raise the BSB as required, using the levers present on mobile power pack trolley and BSB cylinder. Insert both pins in the BSB assembly after aligning the holes. Turn OFF the mobile power pack engine after use and remove hoses.
Change the mode of bridge end assembly from launched mode to transportation mode using lever handle provided on the BEM-1 and lock it using its locking pin.
Connect the hoses of mobile power pack trolley to BEM-2 at home bank. Change the lever position of BEM-2 to RAMP UP position.

Turn ON the mobile power pack engine manually using the recoil starter. Raise the ramps to its maximum cylinder stroke on the home bank by operating the lever on mobile power pack trolley. Turn OFF the mobile power pack engine after use and remove hoses.

Move the LV approx. 8 m from launched bridge. Engage the PTO. Level the launching system as per section 2.4.2. Place CV-5 to the right hand side at approximate gap of 1 m. Unfold the MHD and attach lifting beam to crane.
Remove the lock from ramp assembly. Attach the slings to the first ramp assembly. Lift the ramp assembly and place it on CV-5. Repeat this step for the second ramp also.

Raise the RSS and lock it at home bank manually. Lift the Stabilizer cylinder in upward direction. Bring the launcher vehicle in reverse mode near the launched bridge at 4.4 m away from the launch site.

Extend the launching platform at far bank. Connect the hoses of launching system to BSB of home bank. Remove the locking pins of BSB. Raise the BSB as required, using the PVG-2. Insert locking pins of BSB to lock. Disconnect the hoses of launching system and kept it at prescribed location. Retract the launching platform to original position.

Connect the nose extension assembly of the home bank to the screw rod of the launching system and lock it using locking pin. Change the mode of bridge end assembly from launched mode to transportation mode using lever handle provided on the BEM-2 and lock it using its locking pin.
Lift the mobile power pack trolley and kept it on CV-5.
Extend the Sliding platform cylinder to hold the flap end of BEM-2 in the hook of launching platform.
Attach the chain slings which connect the BEM-2 to bridge pushing assembly. Remove the bridge to nose locking pin and pull the bridge module towards the LV.
Insert the bridge to nose locking pin to lock BCM-5 to NEM-2. Attach the chain slings of lifting beam to the BEM-2. Remove the chain slings which connect BEM-2 to the bridge pushing assembly.
Lift and place the BEM-2 on CV-5 such that flap is facing towards the carrier vehicle end.
In same process, remove the all bridge modules from the bridge assembly and place them on their respective CVs as per their stowage assemblies.

cell.text: Make sure all locking pins as per CV stowage assembly to be perform before moving CVs. Make sure that the ratchet lashing belts are applied and tightened.

item.text: Loosen the turn buckles. Detach the turn buckles from NEM and attach to BSB base structure at both banks. Remove the locking pin connecting the nose extension assembly and screw rod of launching system.

clause.title: Nitrogen Charging for Accumulator
clause.para: Hydraulic accumulators are specifically designed to store and discharge pressurized fluid as needed. Hydro pneumatic accumulators are charged with nitrogen which is separated from the fluid by a diaphragm. There are risks involved when working with high press gases and fluids on no account must any welding soldering or any mechanical work be carried out on the accumulator shell. work on systems employing hydraulic accumulators must only be carried out once the pressure in the fluid and or the gas have been released. Hydro pneumatic accumulators need to be pre-charged with an inert gas in order to work at all selection of the correct gas pressure.
The nitrogen charging for the accumulator requires a nitrogen filled cylinder, charging kit, hose, 6 mm allen key and calibrated pressure gauge with maximum range limit of 250 bar to 400 bar.

item.text: Rotate the allen screw of accumulator-top in anticlockwise direction (half turn only), using 6 mm allen key to loosen the screw for nitrogen charging.
Mount the nitrogen charging kit on the accumulator-top. Tighten the bottom socket of the charging kit to the accumulator-top manually by rotating it the clockwise direction.

cell.text: The release valve of the nitrogen charging kit must be in closed condition and tightened completely before mounting the charging kit on the accumulator.

item.text: Connect the hose from nitrogen filled cylinder to charging kit.
Tighten the hoses at both ends. Make sure that no loose ends are observed.
Make sure that the calibrated pressure gauge with maximum range limit of 250-400 bars is assembled to the charging kit for checking the pressure after charging.
Open the spindle present on the nitrogen filling cylinder (rotate in anticlockwise direction) to inflow nitrogen into the accumulator.
Rotate the spindle of the charging kit in anticlockwise direction slowly for filling nitrogen in the accumulator.
Keep inspecting the pressure gauge. Turn OFF the spindle of charging kit by rotating it in clockwise direction, once the required level of 170-180 bar has reached.
Turn OFF the spindle present on the nitrogen filling cylinder by rotating it in clockwise direction to stop the nitrogen flow.
Make sure both the spindles (nitrogen cylinder and charging kit) are completely closed.
Open the release valve of the charging kit to release the excess nitrogen fluid present in the hose itself.

figure.title: Release Valve Location on Charging Kit

item.text: Turn OFF the release valve.
Remove the hose and remove the charging kit from the accumulator.
Tighten the allen screw of the accumulator-top using 6 mm allen key. Make sure that the screw is completely tightened and no leakage is observed.
Rotate the allen screw of accumulator-top in anticlockwise direction (half turn only), using 6 mm allen key to loosen the screw for nitrogen charging.
Mount the nitrogen charging kit on the accumulator-top. Tighten the bottom socket of the charging kit to the accumulator-top manually by rotating it the clockwise direction.

cell.text: The release valve of the nitrogen charging kit must be in closed condition and tightened completely before mounting the charging kit on the accumulator.

cell.text: Welding must be done through the qualified welder. Welding qualification must be done as per ASME Sec IX or AWS D 1.1

item.text: A detailed technological procedure based upon the actual defect to be prepared for each defect. The procedure must be approved by the technical officer of the depot / plant / performing the repairs.

Absolute cleanliness of the area where welding is done is of paramount importance. All necessary care to be taken to avoid contamination by dust and moisture. Welding must be done in covered fabrication shops.
The surfaces to be welded and the filler metal is free from moisture, grease, oil films, oxides, fume condensates or foreign matter.

When preparing for a repair, it is necessary to discriminate between defects caused by normal operations and those caused by accidents and emergencies. Regardless of whether the repair will be completed by the base workshop depot or that of the field workshop, causes and circumstances leading to the defect to be painstakingly determined. This is necessary, both for carrying out the repair satisfactorily and for selecting the manufacturing materials, the welding technology and for quality inspection procedures.

The welding procedures used for a repair must always be based on the welding technology used in manufacturing the new part. All traces of corrosion, grease, moisture and chips to be removed from edges of prepared plates for welding.

Edge chamfering, welding gaps, overlaps, flatness, etc. must meet the specifications laid down in the welding procedures. Each spot welding of parts and assemblies to be carried out with proper electrodes and by proper technological procedures and the dimensions of tacks must not exceed the dimensions of the final weld either in thickness or in length and welding operation must be carried out in places protected against wind and rain and at environment temperatures above 0 °C.

All steel components / parts to be welded by manual metal arc welding / metal inert gas (MIG) / SMAW / MAG process of welding. However, Tungsten Inert gas (TIG) welding process may be used for welding as permitted by the weld map document and WPS / PQR. Flat welding is preferable to positional welding.

Welds are accepted on the basis of external inspection and check with a template having specified dimensions. Strength welds are tested by the electro-magnetic flow detection method with liquid indicators as specified in the welding procedure. No cracks in the weld and fusion are permitted.
The weld must be made symmetrically with satisfactory dimensions and surface. No burn off and undercut is permitted at the time of fusion between base metal and the weld metal.

Defective welds must be cut out with a cold chisel or removed by grinding up to the base material and re-welded. In this case no tack welding is permitted. The weld repair must be approved in advance by the responsible technical officer.

Weld deformations to be flattened in hot or cold state. Use only flattening tools which cannot damage the material of the product. Material cannot be heated up to more than a dark red color. It is not permitted to heat parts and components, which has been heat treated during the manufacturing process.
Burnt through spots are repaired from the side of the weld root.
Deformed main components of the hydraulic system of the launching mechanism to be repaired only in a maintenance depot under the supervision of the Unit Technical Officer (UTO).
Use suitable means to protect the following elements from effects of welding heat and burrs cylinders, electrical cables, hydraulic piping by wrapping in wet rags, fire proof screens etc.

When handling the electrodes, avoid at all costs that the electrode touches the surface of extended cylinder piston rods, so as not to damage their polished surfaces / it is recommended to wrap such parts with rags or thick paper.

Welding electrodes used for welding HSLA-700MC, S690 steel plates to be, hydrogen controlled low alloy, high tensile electrodes conforming to SFA5.5/SFA5.5M/E11018M for manual metal arc / SMAW welding and SFA 5.28/SFA 5.28M ER110S-1/ER76S-1 for GTAW process. Alternately, conforming to SA A5.28/SFA A5.28M of class E110CK4/E110T15 or alternately equivalent to be used for welding HSLA 700 / HSLA 700 to HSLA 1100E by MAG / welding.
Welding electrodes used for Welding HSLA 1100E Steel plates to conform AWS specification to AWS class E131 K4H4 EN ISO 18276-A, T89 4 Z Mn2NiCrMo M M21 1 H5 by GMAW process.

Welding electrodes used for welding of grade E350 of quality ‘C’ or any P1 grade as per ASME Section IX, 2C conforming to AWS specification SFA: 5. 1/SFA 5.1M AWS Class: E7018-1 by SMAW process and SFA 5.18/ SFA 5.18M of AWS class ER70S-6/ E70C-6M for GMAW process.
Filler alloy used for welding of 6061 aluminum alloys, conforming to AWS specification SFA-5.10/SFA 5.10M and AWS Class ER5356.

clause.title: Preparation of Work
clause.para: The parts to be welded are effectively pre-cleaned (at welded location only) with a stainless steel brush before welding.

clause.title: Pre-cleaning
clause.para: Dirt, grease, machining lubricants or any organic matter must have removed from the areas to be welded by cleaning with suitable mechanical wire brushing / cloth / solvent vapor degreasing if required. Chemical cleaning can be done with solvents like Butyl alcohol, Phosphoric acid, Trichloroethylene, Acetone or Carbon Tetrachloride if required.

clause.title: Precautions
clause.para: Precautions are necessary when pre-cleaning with trichloroethylene or carbon tetrachloride as phosgene gas may be formed during welding from traces of these chemicals remaining on the job. To avoid this gas formation, it is important to make sure that the parts are completely dry before welding. The work piece must not be handled with bare hands or dirty gloves after pre-cleaning. The GTAW filler metal used for welding also pre-cleaned preferably by dry steel wool to remove the naturally forming oxide thereon.

clause.title: Mechanical Cleaning by Wire Brushing
clause.para: The joint areas to be vigorously brushed using a stainless steel wire brush. For hand operated brushing, widest possible brushes are used vigorously on the area to be welded. After brushing, the joint area blown clear of all particles using a cloth/ compressed air jet, which must be clean and free of moisture. In multi-run welds, cleaning by wire brush is to be carried out after completion of each run.

clause.title: Spot Checks
clause.para: Frequent inspection including spot checks using white cotton swabs dipped in solvent must be carried out to ensure complete decontamination of the areas to be welded.

clause.title: Preheating
clause.para: Pre-heating of steel alloy of lower thickness section is generally not necessary. However, pre-heating may be necessary when welding of higher thickness sections above 20 mm thick to be joined by butt or fillet weld or to achieve a heat balance between dissimilar thicknesses. Temperature to be checked using sensitive pyrometers or temperature sensitive crayons. However, when the base metal temperature is below 32 0F (0 0C), the base metal is preheated to a minimum of 70 0F (20 0C) and the minimum inter-pass temperature is to maintained during welding as per approved WPS.

clause.title: Repair of Cracks
clause.para: Cracks must be repaired very carefully and in compliance with the following principles:

item.text: Using a suitable indicating method, determine the shape and extent of the crack. Fix the crack ends by drilling holes through the entire thickness of the plate. The hole diameter is to be equal approximately the material thickness.
Chamfer the edges of the drilled holes under 45-degree angle. Start to re-weld from the center of the crack towards its ends and weld at low current ratings.
Arriving at the end of the crack route, weld to the surface of the repaired part and grind off the thus generated convex bead.
If any crack observes in weld of bridge, it has to be repaired as per standard repair procedure.
If crack is observed in parent metal, it has to be reported to design agency.

clause.title: Repair of Painted Surface
clause.para: Maintenance of painting to be carried out as per procedure laid down in IS-1477 (Part II)

item.text: Clean up the painted surfaces to check for any peeling, damages / or any other visible defects.
Wash those areas with detergent solution and rinse with fresh water to remove oil grease and other dirt and dry thereafter.
If the base metal is not exposed the damaged coating area to be applied with same Primer / MIO followed by PU top coat.
In case bare metal is exposed, the damaged / rusted steel surface to be clean locally by power tool / emery paper and painting of that surface is carried out.
Required final thickness to be built up by having 2-3 coats of primer prior to PU Top coat.

cell.text: All hydraulic plumbing must be painted as per color codes. Reflective tape must be pasted at appropriate location on structures for transportation.

clause.title: Authorization
clause.para: Carry out the minor repairs by the system crew but more complicated repairs to be carried out by qualified workshop fitters in cooperation with the system crew. The later repairs are usually made in a maintenance depot.

clause.title: Authorised Repair by Crew
clause.para: The crew is authorised to carry out following repairs:

item.text: To flatten the deformed parts on the nose modules, bridge modules and launching mechanism subassemblies.
To replace the sheared bolts.
To replace the bearings, if any.
To replace common nuts, bolts, washers, cotter pins / split pins.
To replace the pins in the joints and securing and locking pins, identical ones taken from the stock of spare parts.
To replace filter elements.
To replace hydraulic oil.

clause.title: Authorised Repair by Crew Under Supervision

item.text: Only authorized crew to carry out following work under the supervision of a qualified workshop fitter:
To replace the damaged hydraulic elements.
The crew is forbidden to carry out the work connected with the repairs or stripping which is to be carried out solely by the qualified workshop fitter.
Repair and stripping of the hydraulic cylinders, functional elements of the hydraulic system including the rotary joints and electrical equipment inclusive of all types of boxes.
Repair of the major deformations with element heating / by oxyacetylene flame / on bridge top decks.
Welders qualified by a competent authority are only authorized to repair the cracks in the bridge track way.

Welding on the subassemblies is to be carried out only by welders qualified by the competent authority and trained by the manufacturer. More complex hydraulic elements, etc. must be forwarded for repair to the base workshop or the manufacturer.

cell.text: For PVGs and pumps, it is recommended overhauling to be carried out at OEM premises OR in presence of OEM representative suitably.
Safety regulations is observed during all crew actions with the bridging system i.e. its operation, alignment and adjustment and during repairs.

Climbing upon the bridging system permitted only when the bridge has been laid on the ground. Exceptions to this rule are permissible only during emergencies and for the shortest possible time. The driver must disconnect the PTO and stop the engine and switch OFF the system operation.

The driver can switch on the hydraulic pump drive and / or start the engine only upon a direct order issued by the commander or by the person responsible for the operation / a qualified workshop fitter. Such a person is required to issue a warning to all persons employed on adjustments or repairs.

All persons are required to move over the LV with special caution while the PTO engaged and pump is running. It is forbidden to move over the structure in the vicinity of the propeller shaft or under carriage gearbox, as there is a risk of being caught by rotating shafts in case of accidental slipping. The same applies for the PTO shaft connecting to the hydraulic pump drive. Before the vehicle engine started or the hydraulic pump drive switched ON every person is required to move away from the neighbourhood of the said shafts and to remove all loose objects.

text.b: Safety regulations for handling the fabricated components:

cell.text: All the sharp corners of the fabricated components / parts / subassemblies / assemblies to be ground / machined to avoid the injuries to the individual / workers during handling of the fabricated parts.
Safety regulations for work with cranes:

Disassembly and assembly operations in which a crane employed must be carried out in conformance with safety regulations specified in the crane operating manual, in other regulations and standards. This applies for both handling the crane and slinging loads.

NOTE: When several persons participate in alignment and / or repair work, one of them / usually the commander or the qualified workshop fitter / is assigned as the person responsible for keeping to the safety regulations.
Detach or strip individual systems and assemblies only if inevitable for completing the repair.

Assess the required detachment and stripping operations, prepare tools, utensils, ancillaries and fixtures and eventually ropes and cables, a crane and other bridge vehicle before starting actual work.
When stripping assemblies into subassemblies and parts mark their relative positions to facilitate and speed up the re-assembly.
When stripped cleaned and degreased individual components preserve them with preserving oil for the period until re-assembly.
i) Hydraulic elements: i.e. cylinders, motor and various pipes to be plugged after detachment and the rubber plugs left in place until reassembly.
ii) After the QDC is disconnected, plug the male and female QDC with dust cap during maintenance.
If plugs drop out from pipes during their storage, wash the unplugged pipes with trichloroethylene and blow them with compressed air before refitting them.

Stripped and detached sealing gaskets, seals, split pins, washers and other minor parts are always replaced by new parts for assembly. The same applies to bolts and nuts with damaged heads / threads. Use only correctly sized spanners for tightening bolts and nuts to prevent damaging their head.
When taken down, pins, pivots, sealing, gaskets etc. check them visually and replace them by new parts from the stock of spare parts if worn.

When completed a repair, carry out corresponding adjustment and alignment e.g. springs, limit switches, check for leaks / plugs, sealing and joint tightness / bolts and nuts and if a major part or system of the bridge laying vehicle is repaired, check out the function of the repaired part of connected system.

Dip new sealing gaskets / O-rings, other sealing gaskets / made of rubber for at least 20 minutes in the same type of oil or fluid which they are going to seal off before fitting them to the part / hydraulic fluid, gear oil etc.

Pins of connector are protected against dust, water and mechanical damage. If connector found damaged, remove it, clean, soldered and reinstalled. Make sure to use cap and chain provided with connector.

clause.title: Introduction
clause.para: MB is transported by road only. It may be either with its own or by transported in trailer truck.

clause.title: Transportation by Road (With its Own)
clause.para: MB is capable of self-movement by road for all practical purposes. It is always easier and faster to transport the equipment by road, however, during long distance travel sufficient spares viz. tyres, tubes, clutch plates and fan belts are required to be carried.
Following checks are required to be carried out before transportation:

item.text: Check engine oil.
Check clutch oil.
Check charging of batteries.
Check diesel.
All electrical cables, hoses, etc. are tied / clamped properly.
Transportation locks of LV’s are properly locked.
Transportation locks (lashing belts) of CV’s are properly locked.
Crane is properly in folded condition.

clause.title: Transportation by Road (Trailer Truck)
clause.para: MB can be transport over trailer. Following checks are required to be carried out before transportation:

item.text: For transportation purpose 40 ft. SLBT (Semi Low Bed Trailer) open condition hydraulic axle type trailer to be use.
Proper space (length, width) is available in trailer platform.
All government norms of transportation to be check and followed.
One (1) vehicle (either LV or CV) to be transport per trailer.
All the bought out items are correctly packed so as to avoid any damage to the equipment.
The spares and accessories must be packed in boxes for road transportation and packing notes to be stick over each box.
Ramp arrangement is to be provide for trailer to loading and unloading.
LVs and CVs to be lock with chains on trailer as per transportation scheme given in Figure 241, Figure 242, Figure 243 and Figure 244.
After loading of LV or CV, cover it properly using tarpaulin.

All the boxes to be suitably marked with the details of destination as well as the dispatcher.
The proper packing notes duly certified by the inspection authority to be placed in each box.
All finished holes and pins to be greased before packing.

clause.title: Preservation Procedure
clause.para: When temperature, and moisture conditions are such that condensation may take place on components. As far as possible effort must be made to store the material in heated and ventilated storage area. Care to be taken preserving all the components so as not to get spoiled. Mating interface surfaces to be properly covered with oil / grease or respective preservative materials, and the components to be stored properly. Extra care to be taken to preserve the seal so that they do not get any surface damage / or spoiled from environmental conditions.

item.text: No special storage instructions or facilities are required for storage. But still, following points to be ensure while storing:
The vehicle parking brakes are applied.
Wooden blocks are put on vehicle wheels.
In case of storage for a long duration, vehicle may be jacked up and wooden supports must be put underneath front and rear axles.
Vehicles to be store in a shelter.

If during storage for a long duration vehicle is made to stand on its wheels, then specified tyre pressure is maintained and tyres must periodically shifted slightly so as to avoid weakening of tyres at one particular point.
The instructions for storage of the equipment given are as follows:
Proper shade or coverage is provided to each subsystem before integration to protect them from environment or other injurious subsystems.
Vehicle duly integrated with launching system and hydraulic system is kept in proper shade.
After completion of the above work, disconnect all the hydraulic and electrical connections wherever applicable.
To prolong the life of ropes, it is necessary to protect them against slings, sharp bends and soil impurities to avoid damage of rope by pressing the particles of soil in between the strand of ropes.

clause.title: Outer Inspection to be Performed
clause.para: The outer inspection to be performed under following conditions:

item.text: Inspection to be done once in a week, when storing under roofs / shades.
Inspection to be done twice in week, when storing exceptionally in an open air.
Inspection to be done after heavy rain, storm and wind every time.
Inspection of impurities and intactness of preservation by the preserving coatings.
Inspection of intactness of seals, locking of cabin and toolboxes, locking of covers and fastening of removable accessories.

clause.title: Inner Inspection with Functional Testing
clause.para: The inner inspection of system is to be performed once in a month / twice in a month as required along with the inspection of following:

item.text: Engine running and tightness of the fuel circuit system.
Operation of electric equipment’s.
Tightness of hydraulic, electric and air system of vehicle, bridge a respectively.
Correct functioning of hydraulic and electric system.
Condition of all joints, sealing and rubber parts.
After completion testing and inspection of subsystems must be stored back.

clause.title: Storage of Hydraulic Fittings
clause.para: The hydraulic fittings are stored as per the size; make sure fitting are not mixed together. The hydraulic fittings are blackbodies hence they have more resistance towards corrosion when exposed in air. Fittings is stored in storeroom and the threaded portion must have proper plastic caps so that the threads are not get damaged.

clause.title: Storage of Hydraulic Hoses
clause.para: Hoses are adversely affected by temperature, humidity, zone, sunlight, oil, solvents, corrosive liquid and fumes, insects, rodents and radioactive material. The hydraulic hoses are not stored in sharp bend condition, in stored condition shelf life of hoses are tracked. Storage area is relatively cool, dark, and free of dust, dirt dampness and mild dew. The hoses are stored as per size and according to the end fittings and length.

clause.title: Storage of Hydraulic Seals and Rubber Products

item.text: Seals are often stored as spare parts for prolonged periods. With a few simple precautions, the shelf life of these products are considerably lengthened.
Seals are stored where they are safe from damage by external influences. Deformation, in particular, is avoided during storage.

Under the influence of various external factors e.g. heat, moisture, light, oxygen, ozone and as a result of contact with liquid media the properties of certain materials may change. For example, deformation, aging and weathering causes deterioration of the original mechanical and physical properties, depending on the material and shape of the parts.
Fundamental instructions on storage, cleaning and maintenance of rubber products and seal elements are described in international standards.

clause.title: Storage of Hydraulic Filters, Pump and Cylinders

item.text: Store hydraulic filters, pump and cylinders indoors in a clean, and dry area.
Protect all exposed metal parts. Apply grease on the internal surfaces of cylinder eye / clevis bushes or bearings. Pump drive shafts are wrapped in oil-impregnated tape.

Plug the component’s port connections with plastic plugs. Plastic plugs don’t provide the same sealing integrity as their metal counterparts are easily removed both of which are resulted in contaminated ingression.
Hydraulic items like filters, pump and cylinders are stored on proper packing material like wooden planks.
Correct packing / cushioning has to be provided in the boxes to prevent movement of spares and accessories in the boxes during transportation.
Reusable type of boxes is used with facility to lock and seal the boxes for independent transportation by road.
All the boxes are suitably marked giving the details of destination as well as the dispatcher.
Proper packing notes duly certified by the inspector must be placed in each boxes.
Boxes are inspected by the inspector before they are used for storage of equipment.
Inspection of impurities and intactness of preservation by preserving coatings to be checked periodically.

Inspection for condition of fuel tank and oil tank, oil fillings, closing of air inlet openings, condition of electric equipment, condition of the all subsystems and total condition of
anti-corrosion or anti-fungal protection are to be checked once in a month.
Engine running and tightness of the fuel circuit system.
Condition of all joints, sealing and rubber parts.
All spares and accessories boxes of the subsystems to be kept in stored room.

clause.title: Unpacking
clause.para: If packing found perished, then same to be removed and to be checked for any damages. While unpacking of the hydraulic items e.g. seals, valves, hoses etc., follow instructions mentioned on the box. Knife or blade not to be used during unpacking. Inspect all the equipment and subassemblies for any external damages, loosening of components immediately after unpacking.

clause.title: Preservation
clause.para: All assemblies, subassemblies and special tools are painted as per the standard painting procedure and preserved from environmental condition. All assemblies, subassemblies, spare parts and tools and accessories etc. to be stored in a dry place clear off the ground. When temperature and moisture conditions are such that condensation may occur, material to be stored in ventilated storage area. Oil and greasing to be carried out at all lubrication points as per schedule given in maintenance manual.

clause.title: Packing and Marking
clause.para: All spares, tools and accessories etc. are correctly packed and to be kept in prescribed boxes and necessary marking is carried out for identification of respective store.
